title: 9.3 Chemical periodicity of other elements: Using periodic trends to predict the properties of an element and to identify an unknown element

q.Q1: Q1. Germanium is below silicon in Group 14. Predict the formula of its oxide and of its chloride, and say how you decided.

q.Table: Q4. In which group is the element most likely to be?

q.Q5: Q5. Element Q is in Period 3. It is a solid that conducts electricity. Its chloride, QCl₂, is a white solid with a high melting point that dissolves in water to give a solution of pH 6.5. Identify Q and give two reasons.
q.Q6: Q6. Element R is in Period 3. Its successive ionisation energies show the first large jump after the fifth electron. Its chloride reacts violently with water. Identify R and predict the formula of its highest oxide.

q.Q7: Q7. Gallium, Ga, is below aluminium in Group 13. (a) Predict the formula of gallium oxide and of gallium chloride. (b) Predict whether gallium oxide is basic, amphoteric or acidic, and give your reason. (c) Predict what you would observe when gallium chloride is added to water, and the approximate pH. (d) Predict whether gallium conducts electricity, with a reason.
